correctness.rationale: In a TCP factorization, the all-ones second Gram matrix has rank one, so each factor vector product lies in its one-dimensional range. Coordinatewise moduli then force each vector contributing to the third Gram matrix to have constant modulus; the unit diagonal normalizes their squared moduli to convex weights, yielding a toroidal decomposition. The converse is the standard toroidal-core construction. The explicit four-dimensional Gram matrix has rank two and the four Hermitian face constraints have determinant minus one, proving extremality and therefore non-toroidality. Fresh exact symbolic reconstruction reproduced the rank, eigenvalues and extremality determinant.
